title: Texas Branch Legal Note: Owner's Statutory Retention Held Back from Past-Due Reconstruction Draw Payments
content:
The owner's statutory retention is held back from a payment that brings a past-due customer-funded draw of a Reconstruction contract current.

**The Texas retention.** For a property whose loss address is in Texas, the owner retains part of the contract price until the Texas statutory retention days after the work is completed (Texas Property Code, Chapter 53); the company's rules take that retention as the Texas owner retention percentage of the contract price, which is 10%, with Texas statutory retention days of 30, which the owner holds back itself from its own payments of the customer-funded draws, while the final draw holds it back on the share of the contract the customer does not fund.

**Held back.** For a Texas property, until 30 days after the substantial completion date have passed, on a tier that withholds no retainage, 10% of the draw's requested amount is held back, and on a tier that withholds retainage, the part of the 10% above the tier's retainage percentage, of the draw's requested amount; for every other property nothing is held back.

**Paid in full.** On a Texas property, until 30 days after the substantial completion date have passed, a customer-funded draw is paid in full when all of it but the statutory retention has been paid; its statutory retention is 10% of its requested amount, on a tier that withholds retainage the part of that percentage above the tier's retainage percentage.

## By agreement (Texas property, within the period)

| Agreement | Tier retainage | Held back, as a share of the draw's requested amount |
|---|---|---|
| Repair Agreement - Minor Repairs | 0% | 10% |
| Standard Rebuild Agreement | 0% | 10% |
| Major Rebuild Agreement | 0% | 10% |
| Full Structural Rebuild Agreement | 5% | 5% |
| Multifamily Unit Rebuild Agreement | 0% | 10% |
| Commercial Interior Rebuild Agreement | 10% | 0% |

## The period

The retention is held back while the contract has no substantial completion date, and after it through the 30th day after the substantial completion date, days counted as calendar days with the completion date itself not counted; from the 31st day nothing is held back.

**Example (hypothetical).** A Texas draw requested at $5,500.00 on an agreement that withholds no retainage, with the contract not yet substantially complete: $550.00 is held back from the payment.
